## Conclusions
- **Sanity check:** MobileCLIP2-B through the teacher pipeline (open_clip tokenizer, PIL bicubic squash-resize)
  scores 71.31, identical to experiment 002 through the deployment wrappers. So the teacher numbers are
  comparable to the student numbers.
- **Zero-shot, bigger is barely better on this task.** The best single model, PE-Core-L/14-336 (~430M params,
  336 px), beats B by only +2.6 points. ViT-H/14-378 (DFN-5B, ~990M) gains +1.3, and MobileCLIP2-L/14 is not
  significantly better than B. The three-model similarity-averaged ensemble is best at 74.19 (+2.9).
- **What this means for distillation:** distilling a zero-shot teacher can close at most a ~3-point gap. The
  bigger lever is probably the domain shift (short, attribute-style object captions) that none of these
  models was trained for, which is what fine-tuning on the RefCOCO-family training set targets (exp 010).
- **Decision:** use PE-Core-L/14-336 (best single model) and the 3-model ensemble as the distillation
  teachers in 011, against the contrastive-only control (010) with identical data and steps.
- **Practical note:** loading teachers while training ran hit a Windows "paging file too small" error; teachers
  are embedded once and cached (`.cache/teacher_sims/`, `.cache/teacher_emb/`), so run them alone. The first,
  interrupted run of this experiment was deleted and rerun from the cache (same code, same results).
